topic: The minimax fraction of the oracle variance-reduction gain that a single committed randomization design can guarantee simultaneously across a finite family of unknown response-structure classes, and the design certified to attain it

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite family of potential-outcome response-structure classes, what is the largest worst-class fraction of the complete-randomization-to-class-oracle variance-reduction gain attainable by one precommitted randomization distribution?

source_refs.claim: Minimax balance requires a specified outcome-function class; without structure, complete randomization is minimax optimal.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.claim: Unknown outcome and covariate ICCs make the locally optimal cluster-trial design unknown, so the authors maximize worst-case relative efficiency over parameter ranges.
source_refs.author: Mary M. Ryan, Denise Esserman, and Fan Li

source_refs.claim: A robustness parameter bounds worst-case ATE MSE while the design balances linear prognostic functions, exposing a robustness-precision continuum.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Savje, Daniel A. Spielman, and Peng Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: Derive the sharp adaptation-index order by carrying out the stated policy-uniform constrained-risk lower-bound route
It does not prove a matching growing-horizon oracle rate, divergent adaptation cost, or a common procedure

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published causal-design results optimize against one specified function class, one robustness parameter, or one parameter rectangle; their relative-efficiency criteria do not normalize each class by its own gain over a common baseline. That gain normalization introduces class-dependent and possibly zero denominators, so ordinary minimax-variance convexity does not directly yield a commitment value. The in-repo polynomial-carryover instance confirms the obstacle: its universal lower exponent and class-aware upper exponent do not match, and no policy-uniform two-class constrained-risk certificate or structure-agnostic attaining design has closed the gap.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample saddle-point or convex-program characterization of the sharp gain fraction, an explicit attaining randomization distribution, and a matching adversarial certificate, with a two-sided asymptotic rate in growing-horizon subclasses.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from covariate balance to response-class-dependent minimax variance and the no-structure complete-randomization benchmark.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: covariate balance can improve precision -> every balance objective encodes a response class -> the oracle design changes with that class -> what fraction of every class-specific oracle gain can one committed design retain?

method_exemplars.technique: Represent assignment laws as mixed strategies and apply minimax duality to covariance-matrix risk, producing primal designs and dual optimality certificates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is the same design-versus-potential-outcomes game with several class-normalized gains instead of one worst-case variance.

method_exemplars.technique: Normalize each candidate design by its locally optimal benchmark and optimize worst-case relative efficiency over unknown design parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the closest causal-trial construction comparing one committed resource allocation with parameter-specific oracles.

method_exemplars.technique: Use distributional-discrepancy bounds for Horvitz-Thompson MSE, then prove a design-based CLT and construct a conservative variance estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An attaining commitment design needs both a covariance-risk certificate and valid inference under its dependent assignments.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the shifted Chebyshev-Lobatto rollout schedule minimize exact worst-case finite-population variance under the true monotone-Bernoulli covariance, rather than only its total-variation envelope?

source_refs.excerpt: If aiming above field, add either an exact-covariance theorem for Gamma_P(p) or an estimator/inference corollary
The open exact-covariance question concerns the exact finite-population monotone-Bernoulli covariance Gamma_P

open_problems.why_unsolved: The proved Chebyshev argument controls an interpolation total-variation envelope and transfers it to exact risk only as an upper bound. The true covariance depends jointly on rollout nodes and the finite potential-outcome schedule, so the extremal-polynomial lower bound for the envelope does not establish exact nested minimax optimality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A covariance-aware minimax theorem proving Chebyshev-Lobatto exact optimality with a matching lower bound, or a regime-specific counterexample together with the actual optimal rollout schedule.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the rollout-polynomial motivation and endpoint-extrapolation setup inherited by the banked proposal.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: unknown network interference obstructs ordinary exposure analysis -> low-order outcomes make the rollout mean polynomial -> staggered measurements identify its endpoint contrast -> which measurement nodes minimize exact design variance?

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the polynomial interpolation estimator and derive its finite-population covariance exactly under nested Bernoulli rollout.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is the exact covariance risk of the same rollout estimator rather than the total-variation relaxation.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the pseudoinverse variance representation for general designs to expose the covariance-aware node-placement objective and its dual.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A pseudoinverse risk formula is the nearest route from low-order rollout identification to exact variance optimization.

open_problems.open_problem: For heterogeneous-Bernoulli bipartite experiments, is the graph-only variance envelope the exact worst-case asymptotic variance over centered bounded potential-outcome schedules, or is it at least uniformly constant-factor sharp?

source_refs.excerpt: Investigate whether V_env is sharp or constant-factor sharp as a worst-case bounded-outcome variance envelope
The observable constant-factor certificate for the low-dimensional surrogate remains the open-ended question.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The current optimization uses a conservative graph-only envelope obtained after discarding sign and cross-arm compatibility information. Exact or constant-factor sharpness requires a coupled quadratic supremum subject to centering, boundedness, and common potential-outcome constraints; without it, an envelope-optimal propensity vector need not be minimax for actual design variance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp equality or uniform two-sided constant-factor bound between the response supremum and the graph envelope, with extremal response schedules and a certified design attaining the induced minimax ratio.

writing_exemplar.why: It is the direct homogeneous-design anchor and supplies the variance-to-design motivation for heterogeneous propensities.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: bipartite interference induces overlapping exposures -> homogeneous Bernoulli Hajek variance is analyzable -> graph heterogeneity motivates unit-specific propensities -> is the optimized graph envelope genuinely minimax for bounded responses?

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the optimization and dual characterization of conservative quadratic variance bounds to test sharpness and construct extremal schedules.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems optimize an observable conservative variance object and must distinguish bound optimality from worst-case sharpness.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the exact Hajek variance decomposition and conservative variance proof from a common propensity to nonidentical propensities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the homogeneous covariance identity against which the heterogeneous envelope must reduce and be calibrated.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact zero-versus-positive rounding-loss frontier for implementable plus-or-minus-one randomization in the two-block interference-homophily covariance SDP as the response-class radius varies at fixed homophily?

source_refs.excerpt: The EXACT zero/positive-loss frontier r_star -- which supportwise contact strata y+z=2/m are genuine transition points

open_problems.why_unsolved: Known results identify cut-exact and iid-exact corners plus one odd-size positive-gap window, but the active support of the reduced conic program changes with response radius and homophily. The transition set can be set-valued, and it is unresolved which contacts with the sign-covariance boundary are genuine implementability transitions rather than changes internal to the relaxed optimizer.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite semialgebraic phase decomposition or explicit frontier function, with if-and-only-if zero-loss criteria, an implementable attaining design on exact cells, and a positive rounding-loss formula elsewhere.

writing_exemplar.why: It is the direct SDP-relaxation anchor and frames the interference, homophily, robustness, and implementability tradeoff.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: network interference turns assignment covariance into a design variable -> the elliptope gives a tractable SDP relaxation -> realizable sign covariances can fall short -> where exactly does implementability loss switch from zero to positive?

method_exemplars.technique: Use cut-polytope and Bernoulli-correlation realizability constraints to characterize which reduced covariance points correspond to actual randomization laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The frontier is exactly an elliptope-versus-sign-covariance feasibility boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt SDP hierarchy and cardinality-constrained rounding certificates to separate exact implementability cells from positive-loss cells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unresolved object combines sign-vector realization with a global treatment-balance constraint.

open_problems.open_problem: How do the minimax-optimal committed randomization design and its guaranteed oracle-gain fraction change when permutation or block invariance holds only approximately rather than exactly?

source_refs.claim: The finite-sample minimax characterization assumes exact permutation invariance and explicitly leaves approximate invariance as an open extension.
source_refs.author: Yuehao Bai

source_refs.claim: Complete randomization is minimax for permutation-symmetric outcome classes, while structured nonsymmetric classes generally require another mixed design.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact invariance permits group symmetrization and identifies complete or block randomization as minimax. Under approximate invariance, nature can concentrate a small symmetry defect in directions amplified by a structured assignment covariance. No result supplies a sharp modulus linking that defect to loss relative to the exact-class oracle or locates the transition from complete randomization to blocking or stronger balance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite-sample commitment-value theorem indexed by an explicit approximate-invariance radius, with an attaining randomized design and matching least-favorable approximately invariant response schedules.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames randomization through exact invariance and ends at the approximate-invariance gap.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: permutation invariance creates a symmetric minimax game -> symmetrization makes complete or block randomization optimal -> real response classes are only approximately symmetric -> quantify the best robust design and its price under symmetry defects

method_exemplars.technique: Average assignment and estimation rules over a permutation group and identify least-favorable invariant distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The perturbation theorem would start from this exact symmetrization and quantify the defect caused by approximate invariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent worst-case design variance through assignment covariance matrices and solve the mixed-strategy minimax problem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The covariance formulation can identify the approximately invariant directions driving the transition between randomization regimes.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive a finite-population limit law under restricted randomization and invert its Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian form for design-aware inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Approximately invariant classes may select restricted designs whose limit law is not the complete-randomization CLT.

open_problems.open_problem: Can an exactly half-treated randomization distribution attain the optimal worst-class oracle-gain guarantee while preserving the covariance and tail bounds of distributional-discrepancy designs?

source_refs.claim: The exactly balanced group-size modification of the Gram-Schmidt Walk breaks the update orthogonality, so the paper's analysis does not apply.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Savje, Daniel A. Spielman, and Peng Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Minimax precision can require randomization over more than one complementary assignment pair, and support constraints matter for design-based inference.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact treatment-count balance imposes a global linear constraint on assignments. Enforcing it in Gram-Schmidt-style walks destroys the update orthogonality used for covariance domination and sub-Gaussian tail bounds. Therefore neither the attainable robust gain across response classes nor a matching optimality certificate is known in this practically standard fixed-arm-size design space.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constrained distributional-discrepancy theorem characterizing the sharp gain fraction over exactly balanced assignments and proving matching covariance and tail bounds for a concrete sampling design.

writing_exemplar.why: Its balance-versus-robustness narrative and explicit equal-arm-size limitation lead directly to the question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: dependent randomization balances prognostic covariates -> distributional discrepancy controls robustness -> trials commonly require equal arm sizes -> recover sharp robust-gain guarantees under that hard constraint

method_exemplars.technique: Translate treatment assignment into vector discrepancy and dominate augmented-covariate imbalance covariance by an explicit projection matrix.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested theorem is the exactly balanced analogue of this covariance certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize over assignment covariance matrices subject to randomization and inference-support constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Exact half-treatment is an additional support constraint in the same minimax design game.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate the randomized-pivot walk by a skeletal process and use exchangeable-pair Stein bounds for a CLT and exact limiting variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A constrained walk needs comparable design-based limit theory after its dependence structure changes.

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite menu of linear and nonlinear response-function classes, can one kernelized randomization design guarantee a sharp fraction of every class-specific oracle variance reduction without choosing one kernel or feature map ex ante?

source_refs.claim: The Gram-Schmidt Walk targets linear functions; automatic nonlinear balance through kernels is identified as beyond the paper's scope.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Savje, Daniel A. Spielman, and Peng Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Kernel allocation obtains minimax variance guarantees when response structure is encoded by one chosen function space.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kernel allocation and distributional discrepancy require commitment to one geometry. Summing kernels controls a union only through potentially loose radius inflation, while choosing one kernel loses guarantees for the others. The sharp oracle-gain fraction depends on relative spectra and null spaces of the candidate Gram matrices, and the literature does not characterize this simultaneous approximation problem or an attaining assignment law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A spectral or semidefinite characterization of the sharp simultaneous gain factor for finitely many response-class Gram matrices, with an attaining randomized allocation and a matching least-favorable response construction.

writing_exemplar.why: Its concluding limitation moves directly from linear balance to unresolved nonlinear kernel design.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: linear covariate balance improves precision for linear prognostic structure -> nonlinear structure requires kernels -> the correct nonlinear geometry is unknown at commitment -> retain a sharp fraction of every candidate kernel oracle's gain

method_exemplars.technique: Represent worst-case RKHS imbalance by the kernel Gram matrix and optimize the induced minimax variance through semidefinite relaxation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each response class has this RKHS oracle; the new step is simultaneous approximation across several Gram geometries.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct an assignment distribution whose augmented-feature imbalance covariance is bounded by an explicit projection operator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Kernel feature maps turn the target into a multi-operator distributional-discrepancy problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Obtain exact asymptotic variance and a CLT for randomized discrepancy designs through skeletal-process approximation and Stein's method.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The attaining kernelized design needs limit theory tied to its assignment covariance, not only a worst-case risk bound.

literature_map:
1. Kallus (2018, JRSSB, arXiv:1312.0531) casts covariate balance as minimax variance over a chosen outcome-function class and proves complete randomization minimax without structure.
2. Banerjee, Chassang, Montero, and Snowberg (2020, AER, DOI 10.1257/aer.20171634) formalize the experimenter's tradeoff between subjective balance gains and robust randomization.
3. Johansson, Rubin, and Schultzberg (2021, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12417) show why excessively optimized rerandomization can undermine randomization-based inference.
4. Kallus (2021, JRSSB, arXiv:2005.03151) shows mixed randomization, not one optimized partition, is minimax and incorporates inference-support constraints.
5. Bai (2023, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.10.009) proves minimaxity under exact permutation invariance and explicitly leaves approximate invariance open.
6. Morgan and Rubin (2012, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1207.5625) link rerandomization's realized covariate balance to precision gains.
7. Li, Ding, and Rubin (2018, PNAS, arXiv:1604.00698) derive Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian limits under rerandomization.
8. Li and Ding (2020, JRSSB, arXiv:1906.11291) combine rerandomization with regression adjustment and design-aware inference.
9. Harshaw, Savje, Spielman, and Zhang (2024, JASA, arXiv:1911.03071) give a tunable distributional-discrepancy design, finite-sample MSE bounds, and conservative inference.
10. Harshaw et al. explicitly leave both exact equal-arm-size analysis and automatic nonlinear/kernel balance beyond their result.
11. Chatterjee, Dey, and Goswami (2023, arXiv:2305.12512) prove a randomized-pivot Gram-Schmidt Walk CLT and sharpen its limiting variance via Stein's method.
12. Bai (2022, AER, arXiv:2206.07845) characterizes an optimal matched-pair design indexed by a prognostic score.
13. Cytrynbaum (2021, arXiv:2111.08157) obtains optimal fine stratification using pilot information, leaving no-pilot commitment distinct.
14. Ryan, Esserman, and Li (2023, Statistics in Medicine, arXiv:2302.09138) maximize worst-case relative efficiency across unknown ICCs and multiple trial objectives.
15. These strands treat minimax variance, relative efficiency, robustness, and multiple objectives separately; none identifies the sharp class-oracle gain fraction for one committed causal randomization design.
